{{Use British English|date=October 2026}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=October 2026}}

'''Henry Foner''' ({{Langx|he|הנרי פונר}}; born 1932) is an Israeli chemist and author of a book about the ''[[Kindertransport]]'' that saved his life as a child just prior to [[World War II]] as the Nazis added territory in Europe.<ref name=postcards>
{{cite web 
| title = Postcards to a Little Boy: A Kindertransport Story
| publisher = Holocaust History Museum Yad Vashem
| place = Jerusalem
| url = https://store.yadvashem.org/en/postcards-to-a-little-boy-16
| access-date = 19 January 2017}}</ref>

==Background==

Foner was born "Heinz Lichtwitz" (nickname "Heini") in 1932 in Germany. In 1937, his mother died, so his grandparents helped raise him.  His grandfather was Ernst Lichtwitz, owner of a printing press.<ref name=crif>
{{cite news
| first = Barry
| last = Davis
| title = Cartes Postales à un petit garçon
| publisher = Conseil Représentif des Institutions juives de France
| url = http://www.crif.org/fr/alireavoiraecouter/cartes-postales-%C3%A0-un-petit-gar%C3%A7on/38318
| date = 21 March 2016
| access-date = 20 January 2017}}</ref>  Henry lived with his father, Max Lichtwitz and his mother, Ilse Lichtwitz née Badt in Berlin.<ref name=crif /> A few months after ''[[Kristallnacht]]'', he was sent to the United Kingdom and arrived on February 3, 1939, in Swansea, Wales, to live with Morris and Winifred Foner, to whom he referred as his uncle and aunt. His father was sent to [[Auschwitz concentration camp]] on December 9, 1942, and died a week later.<ref name=postcards /><ref name=crif /><ref>
{{cite news
| first = Tina
| last = Bellon
| title = Auschwitz guard's death deprives survivors of justice they hoped for
| publisher = Reuters
| url = https://www.reuters.com/article/us-germany-nazi-trial-victims-idUSKCN0X50XB
| date = 8 April 2016
| access-date = 20 January 2017}}</ref><ref name=independent>
{{cite news
| first = Donald

| title = Goodbye to Berlin: Postcards from Nazi Germany tell story of the Kindertransport
| publisher = Independent
| url = https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/world-history/goodbye-to-berlin-postcards-from-nazi-germany-tell-story-of-the-kindertransport-8665473.html
| date = 22 June 2013
| access-date = 20 January 2017}}</ref><ref>

==Career==

Foner served in the [[British Army]] in Egypt and in Sudan from 1953 to 1955. He obtained a doctorate in chemistry from [[University of Leeds]].{{citation needed|date=February 2020}}

==Personal==

Foner and his wife Judith married in 1960.<ref name=independent /> They have three children and eight grandchildren.

In 1968, Foner and his wife  moved to [[Jerusalem]], Israel.  Although the UK saved his life, he considered Israel his homeland.<ref name=postcards /><ref name="badischez">{{cite news|url=http://www.badische-zeitung.de/ausland-1/verschickung-juedischer-kinder-trennung-aus-liebe--83873608.html|title=Verschickung jüdischer Kinder: Trennung aus Liebe|access-date=20 January 2017|publisher=Badische Zeitung}}</ref>

In 2016, regarding the death of [[Ernst Tremmel]], a guard at Auschwitz, he commented:<ref>
{{cite news
| title = Supervivientes de Auschwitz lamentan la muerte de Ernst Tremmel antes del juicio
| publisher = Europa Press
| url = http://www.europapress.es/internacional/noticia-supervivientes-auschwitz-lamentan-muerte-ernst-tremmel-antes-juicio-20160408124629.html
| date = 8 April 2016
| access-date = 20 January 2017}}</ref><ref>
{{cite news
| title = Auschwitz guard death deprives survivors of justice
| publisher = Terra
| url = https://noticias.terra.com.br/morte-de-guarda-de-auschwitz-priva-sobreviventes-de-justica,f9c62996cf465cc6cb5ce15ed1065563acc3bucm.html
| date = 8 April 2016
| access-date = 20 January 2017}}</ref>
<blockquote>There can never be a full sense of closure. For me, it does not make sense - you can not recover what was stolen.</blockquote>

==Works==
* Foner's book ''Postcards to a Little Boy'' chronicles his experience as a ''Kindertransport'' child.<ref name=postcards />
* ''Postcards to a Little Boy:  A Kindertransport Story'' (2013)<ref name=postcards />
